column1: # Cross-language calendar-time golden table (gh#98).
# The OCaml compiler (ocaml/lib/compiler/expander.ml: parse_iso_date /
# days_of_date / parse_date_to_float) and the Rust runtime
# (rust/crates/ir/src/caltime.rs: parse_iso_date / rata_die /
# date_to_internal) independently parse ISO dates and convert them to
# internal time. They MUST agree on exactly which strings parse and on the
# resulting day offset / internal-t, or a date() literal that compiles on
# one side produces a different time on the other (the §5.6 two-parser
# failure mode the typed-time proposal flagged).
# Both ocaml/test/test_caltime_golden.ml and
# rust/crates/ir/tests/caltime_golden.rs read THIS file and assert the
# rows. Keep it as the single source of truth.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   origin       ISO origin date (anchored t=0)
#   date         ISO date to convert (may carry surrounding whitespace)
#   time_unit    days | weeks | months | years
#   expect       accept | reject
#   delta_days   integer rata_die(date) - rata_die(origin); "-" for reject rows
#   t            internal time = delta_days / days_per_unit(time_unit); "-" for reject rows
# Every value was computed from the OCaml implementation and hand-checked
# against the proleptic-Gregorian calendar (leap rules, month lengths).
origin
# 2020 is a leap year (div 4, not div 100): Jan 1 -> Dec 31 = 365 days.
# Full leap year = 366 days.
# 2021 is not a leap year: full year = 365 days.
# 2000 is a leap year (div 400): Jan(31) + Feb(29) = 60 days to Mar 1.
# 1900 is NOT a leap year (div 100, not div 400): Jan(31) + Feb(28) = 59.
# ── Month boundaries (Feb length leap-aware) ─────────────────────────────
# Feb 28 -> Mar 1 spans Feb 29 in a leap year: +2 days.
# Feb 28 -> Mar 1 in a non-leap year: +1 day.
# ── Dates near / at the proleptic-Gregorian epoch (<= 1583 CE) ────────────
# 1583 is not a leap year: Jan 1 -> Dec 31 = 364 days.
# ── Negative deltas (date before origin) ─────────────────────────────────
# 28 days = 4 weeks exactly.
# A full leap year in 'years units: 366 / 365.2425 = 1.002073965...
# Operational anchor used by the SIA golden models (2013 origin).
# ── Zone designators MUST be rejected (gh#846) ────────────────────
# A bare date is already a civil day with no timezone semantics, so an
# offset is information camdl does not model. Both parsers refuse it rather
# than discarding it, which would silently change what the cell says.
# The civil date the rejected cells reduce to is of course still accepted:
# ── Surrounding whitespace is trimmed ────────────────────────────────────
# ── Out-of-range / malformed dates MUST be rejected (gh#98 C6) ───────────
# Day 30 of February does not exist.
# Month 13 does not exist.
# Feb 29 in a non-leap year does not exist.
# Day 00 does not exist.
# Day 31 of April does not exist (April has 30 days).
# A time-of-day suffix is not supported (v1 accepts a bare date only).
